one_month_reasoning: The one big scheduled event inside the window is the Q3 2026 report on Wednesday 2026-10-28 (release ~4:05pm ET, call 4:30pm ET; company release of 2026-09-17), so the stock reacts on Oct 29. Management already guided Q3 low on the Q2 call: ~250k postpaid account net adds (down from 396k in Q3 2025) because of temporarily higher account churn from the July rate-plan modernization, service revenue ~$19.3B (+6% y/y, a slowdown from +9% in Q2) and Core Adjusted EBITDA ~$9.4B (+8%). Consensus Q3 EPS is about $2.91 (Alpha Vantage). Because the weak quarter was pre-announced and the Sept 3 8-K reaffirmed 2026 guidance, the swing factor is commentary rather than the print itself: whether the 2027 framework ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) is restated in numbers (management avoided repeating the figures at the Sept 9-10 conferences), any early read on the 2027 shareholder-return authorization (the 2026 one was set on 2025-12-11), and the answer to SpaceX/Starlink Mobile after the 800 MHz Grain deal that knocked the stock down 13.3% on Oct 9. Verizon and AT&T Q3 reports in late October (dates not confirmed by me) will also move the group. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: reversal after an extreme one-day sector selloff, and continuation after news-driven drops at 52-week lows with negative 12-month momentum. I keep the distribution almost symmetric around spot (median ~$149.5, a hair above $148.58 for ongoing buybacks and a pre-lowered bar) with a monthly sigma of ~10.5%, above the ~9.4% (33%/3.5) baseline because the window holds earnings and comes right after a volatility shock.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) 12.0x P/E on FY2027 consensus EPS of $13.94 cut by 5% to $13.24 = $159 and (b) 7.0x EV/EBITDA on $40.0B 2027 Core Adjusted EBITDA (the low end of the $40-41B company target) less $87.6B net debt incl. tower obligations, over 1,072.7M shares = $179. Blended: $169 per share at the 12-month horizon, before ~$4.7 of dividends.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2027 EPS $13.94 consensus x 0.95 haircut = $13.24; x 12.0x = $158.9

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 guidance implies service revenue growth slowing to +6% from +9% (src 1, 8). Management did not restate the 2027 dollar targets at the Sept 9-10 conferences (src 9, 10). SpaceX's terrestrial-carrier plan (src 14, 15) raises promotional risk into 2027. 5% is roughly the gap between the midpoint and low end of the 2027 Core EBITDA target, carried through to EPS.

A 27% premium to the 11-peer median forward P/E, still inside the peer range. TMUS 3Y EPS growth forecast is 17.0% vs a peer median of 8.2% (src 13, 16-26). Reported Q2 service revenue grew +8.9% and Core EBITDA +11.7% (src 1). Weighted diluted shares fell 4.6% y/y, 1,134.8M to 1,082.4M (src 2). The company guides 2027 AFCF of $19.5-20.5B (src 4). PEG at 12x is ~0.7 vs the peer-median ~1.15, so the premium is smaller than the growth gap. 12x sits just above TMUS's own current 11.82x forward P/E (src 13).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 7.0x x 2027E Core Adj. EBITDA $40.0B = EV $280.0B; less net debt $84.1B + tower obligations $3.46B = $87.6B; equity $192.4B / 1,072.67M shares = $179.4

inputs_detail.derivation: The Feb 11 2026 target is $40.0-41.0B (src 4). The Sept 3 8-K says the company 'maintains its ... long-term financial framework' (src 6). I take the low end.

On my basis (net debt plus towers, Core Adjusted EBITDA) TMUS trades at 6.88x LTM: $159.4B market cap + $87.6B = $246.9B over LTM Core EBITDA of $35.9B (8.68+8.445+9.24+9.537; src 2, 13). On the lease-inclusive StockAnalysis basis that peers are quoted on, it trades at 8.06x, a ratio of about 1.17. So 7.0x on my basis is about 8.2x on the peer basis: a ~23% premium to the 6.68x peer median, inside the 4.58-9.72x range. The growth evidence is the same as for the P/E. At a 2027-10 horizon, 2027 EBITDA is close to the LTM figure.

bear.story: Starlink Mobile gains credibility: a fast FCC approval of the Grain 800 MHz transfer, an MVNO or roaming deal with a rival, or aggressive pre-launch pricing. On top of that, a Verizon/AT&T/cable promotional war, Q3/Q4 account adds below the 950k-1.05M 2026 range, and a 2027 framework cut by ~10%. The stock re-rates to Verizon/AT&T-like multiples: ~9x a $12.5 2027 EPS = ~$112.

base.story: Rate-plan churn fades after Q3. 2026 guidance is met, and 2027 is delivered near the low end ($40B Core EBITDA, ~$19.5B AFCF). Buybacks of ~$2B+/quarter keep shrinking the share count. The SpaceX threat stays a 2028+ issue but caps the multiple near ~11.5-12x 2027 EPS (~$13.3-13.9): partial recovery to ~$160 plus ~$4.7 of dividends.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 show phone churn still improving and account adds back above 250k/quarter. The 2027 targets are restated or beaten, and a large 2027 return authorization at depressed prices is announced. The FCC process or a carrier JV defuses the SpaceX threat, and the possible contingent share of Grain's resale proceeds adds cash. The stock re-rates to ~13.5x a ~$14.4 EPS = ~$195, near the summer-2026 trading range.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 2.34x (CHTR) to 15.46x (TU); EV/EBITDA (LTM, lease-inclusive EV) 4.58x (CMCSA) to 9.72x (TU); 11 peers, all as of the 2026-10-09 close.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TMUS today: 11.82x forward P/E (StockAnalysis) and 10.66x FY2027 consensus EPS ($148.58/$13.94); 8.06x LTM EV/EBITDA on the peer (lease-inclusive) basis, or 6.88x LTM and 6.10x 2027-target on my net-debt-plus-towers / Core Adjusted EBITDA basis. Chosen: 12.0x P/E (+27% vs the peer median) and 7.0x EV/EBITDA on my basis (~8.2x on the peer basis, +23%). Both are inside the peer ranges.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium rests on reported, structural growth gaps, not on sell-side outperformance calls. (1) EPS growth: TMUS's 3Y EPS growth forecast is 17.0% vs an 8.2% peer median; the only peer near it, AMX (18%), carries EM currency and country risk and trades 10.9x. (2) Top-line and cash growth are reported: Q2 2026 service revenue +8.9% y/y, Core Adjusted EBITDA +11.7%, and 2023-25 CAGRs of 6% service revenue, 8% Core EBITDA and 15% AFCF (8-K Feb 2026). The 2027 targets of $40-41B EBITDA and $19.5-20.5B AFCF were reaffirmed as a 'framework' on Sept 3. (3) Capital returns shrink the share count 4-5% a year (diluted weighted shares 1,134.8M to 1,082.4M y/y) at leverage of only 2.3x net debt/Core EBITDA vs a 2.5x target. (4) Postpaid phone churn is 0.85% (Q2) vs 0.93% for 2025. The premium is deliberately smaller than the growth gap (PEG ~0.7 vs peer ~1.15) to reflect real offsets: account net adds are decelerating (1,180k in 2025 to a 950-1,050k 2026 guide), the company stopped publishing postpaid phone net adds in 2026, and SpaceX's announced terrestrial-plus-satellite entry is an un-modelled 2028+ risk.

thesis_break_reason: $112 is ~25% below spot and about 8x FY2027 consensus EPS ($13.94), below the Verizon/AT&T forward multiples (8.2x/9.2x) even though TMUS's EPS growth is roughly twice theirs. A trade there would most likely mean the growth premise has broken, not ordinary volatility (that is about 0.9 sigma of annual vol, but it would follow a 13% one-day crash). The likely causes: the 2027 framework ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) withdrawn or cut, a structural price war (account adds below ~200k/quarter, ARPA growth turning negative), or SpaceX/Starlink securing nationwide wholesale access or an MVNO and a near-term launch date. Any of these would argue that the premium to peers no longer holds.

key_uncertainties: How credible and how fast SpaceX/Starlink Mobile is as a fourth terrestrial-plus-satellite carrier. The Grain deal is up to 14 MHz paired 800 MHz, needs FCC approval, and has no announced launch date in the sources I read. Analysts say it still needs an MVNO deal or a macro-tower build.
Whether the 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) survive. They were not restated as numbers at the September conferences.
Account growth is decelerating (Q3 guide ~250k vs 396k a year earlier) and the company no longer discloses postpaid phone net adds, so its growth quality is harder to verify.
The sector-wide de-rating (CHTR 2.3x, CMCSA 5.9x, VZ 8.2x forward P/E) and the rate backdrop. Peer multiples may compress further regardless of TMUS execution.
Capital allocation: spectrum auctions in 2027-28 vs buybacks, about $850M of cash tax on the Grain sale, and the 2.5x leverage target.
The size of any contingent payment from Grain's resale to SpaceX. The 10-Q gives no formula, so it is excluded from value.
Management transition: a new CEO (2025), a new CFO from Feb 2027, a new Chief Enterprise Officer and the departure of the product chief.
reasoning: Price context: TMUS fell 13.3% on 2026-10-09, its worst day since 2011, to a 52-week low of $148.58 after SpaceX agreed on Oct 8 to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz licenses to become a 'major mobile carrier' (NBC, Light Reading). Verizon (-8.7%) and AT&T (-9.8%) fell with it. Before that, the stock had slid from ~$196 to ~$172 after the Q2 print, which guided Q3 account adds down to ~250k on rate-plan-modernization churn, and to ~$165 in mid-September. The primary documents show fundamentals that are slowing at the margin but still the best in the group. Q2 2026 service revenue was +8.9%, Core EBITDA +11.7% and AFCF +4.4%. 2026 AFCF guidance was raised to $18.4-18.8B, and 2026 guidance was reaffirmed on Sept 3. Net debt is $84.1B (2.3x), and shares outstanding are 1,072.7M after a 4-5% annual shrink. Three details the recaps skip. (1) The Q2 10-Q discloses that T-Mobile may share in Grain's future monetisation proceeds from the 800 MHz licenses it sold for $2.9B plus 600 MHz. That is a small offset to the SpaceX threat, but I did not value it because there is no formula. (2) T-Mobile no longer reports postpaid phone net adds (the Q4 2025 release did, at 3.29M for 2025; the 2026 releases report only accounts), and account adds are decelerating. (3) At the Citi and Goldman conferences, management declined to repeat the 2027 dollar targets, stressed 'no MVNO for a LEO operator', and flagged a spectrum capital envelope for 2027-28 on the Q2 call. Valuation: at $148.58 the stock trades at 10.7x FY2027 consensus EPS ($13.94) and ~6.1x the 2027 Core EBITDA target on my basis. My fair value is $169: a 50/50 blend of 12x haircut 2027 EPS ($159) and 7.0x 2027 EBITDA ($179). Both multiples sit inside an 11-peer range (median 9.46x P/E, 6.68x LTM EV/EBITDA), and the premium is argued from a growth gap of 17% vs 8% EPS CAGR. Distribution: I do not assume full convergence within 12 months. A new-entrant narrative (the Iliad/Jio-type fear) plus a sector-wide de-rating usually caps multiples for a while, and momentum is strongly negative (-34% over 1 year). So I centre the 12-month distribution at a median of ~$154: spot plus about a third of the gap to fair value, which is consistent with a 25/50/25 bear/base/bull of $112/$160/$195 (probability-weighted ~$157). I use a lognormal-like spread with sigma ~30% (realised 33%) and slightly fatter left-tail mass at the low strikes for a structural-disruption outcome. Thesis break is $112. Research limits: the T-Mobile IR site and Business Wire returned 403, so the earnings-date release was read via a Finviz mirror. Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were rate-limited (no treasury-yield or daily price check). Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available, so LTM values are used and labelled. Lane share: 11 of 26 sources are in-lane primary documents. The shortfall versus the 60% target comes from the 11 per-peer data pages the mandatory comp table requires; excluding those, 11 of 15 (73%) are primary. No option prices or implied volatility were consulted.
